Questions & Answers

Everything You Might Be Wondering

If your question is not here, message us on WhatsApp — we answer within one working hour.

39 Questions

A Building Surveyor is a qualified professional who assesses the condition of buildings — we inspect, measure and report, but we do not carry out repairs. A contractor does the repair work. Because we do not sell repairs, we have no reason to exaggerate or downplay what we find.
New does not mean defect-free. Most new units have dozens of defects — hollow tiles, poor alignment, leaking joints, electrical faults — that are difficult to spot without training and instruments. The developer is obliged to fix them during the DLP, but only if they are properly identified and reported.
It is not compulsory, but we encourage it. Being there means we can point out findings on the spot and explain what matters most. If you cannot attend, we will walk you through the report afterwards.
We operate across Johor, Melaka, Negeri Sembilan and Selangor — and we are flexible for other locations. Contact us to check availability for your area.
Yes. Every inspector is registered under the Royal Institution of Surveyors Malaysia (RISM) and holds a degree in Building Surveying. Inspections are never subcontracted out to unqualified personnel.
A home inspection focuses on defects in an individual unit, usually during the DLP. A Building Condition Assessment (BCA) evaluates the overall condition of an entire building — structure, services and finishes — and is typically commissioned by JMB/MC, corporations or asset owners.
As soon as you receive your keys, and well before the Defect Liability Period (DLP) expires. During the DLP the developer is obliged to rectify defects at no cost to you — once it lapses, every repair becomes your expense.
The Defect Liability Period is the warranty period after handover during which the developer must rectify defects in your unit. The length is stated in your Sale and Purchase Agreement — check your S&P for the exact period that applies to your property.
Not necessarily, but you should act immediately. Contact us and tell us your DLP expiry date — we will prioritise the booking so your defect list can be submitted while your entitlement is still valid.
They can dispute items, and some will. That is exactly why instrument readings matter — a recorded moisture value or a failed earth test is far harder to dismiss than a written complaint. If items are disputed, we can attend a joint inspection with you.
Not before it is verified. A re-inspection checks each item against your original list and confirms whether the repair was actually done to standard. Cosmetic patch-ups are common, and once you sign off, the item is closed.
Yes, and we record it as a distinct category — "New Defect from Rectification Work". Damage caused during rectification is still the developer's responsibility, and separating it from the original defects makes that clear.
Usually it is the best money you will spend. Hidden defects — waterproofing failure, wiring problems, structural cracks — can cost tens of thousands after you move in. Knowing beforehand lets you negotiate, plan repairs, or walk away.
Yes, and many clients do. Our pre-purchase report includes repair cost estimates and a negotiation points list, so you are discussing figures backed by a professional assessment instead of arguing over impressions.
Yes — that is exactly when a pre-purchase inspection is most useful. Arrange viewing access with the seller or agent, and we will inspect within the agreed scope. Tell us your decision deadline and we will work to it.
Yes. For pre-purchase and sub-sale inspections we provide an estimated cost to rectify each defect found, plus a repair priority list separating what is urgent from what can be deferred.
We inspect within whatever access is permitted and state clearly in the report which areas could not be assessed. A limited inspection is still far better than none — but we will never imply we checked something we did not.
A BCA gives JMB/MC, corporations and asset owners a systematic picture of a building's condition: every element rated, defects prioritised, and maintenance budgeting supported by evidence rather than guesswork.
Anyone whose property sits near upcoming construction, demolition or piling works — and also contractors who want protection against false damage claims. The survey must be done before the works begin to be of any use.
That is one of its main purposes. Once every element is rated and prioritised, you can see which repairs are due now and which can be scheduled — which makes contribution planning far easier to justify to owners.
Yes. Commercial inspections are scoped to your objective — buying, leasing or auditing — and we coordinate site attendance around your operating hours where possible.
Yes, and it is often valuable. A re-assessment compared against an earlier documented baseline shows exactly how conditions have changed and whether past repairs held up.
No. We trace leaks non-destructively using moisture meters and thermal imaging, which detect water through finished surfaces. Hacking only happens afterwards, by your contractor, at the exact point we identify.
It reveals what is behind finished surfaces: hidden moisture, overheating electrical connections, missing insulation, concealed pipe routes and voids behind tiles. It is non-destructive and produces evidence that is difficult to dispute.
Earth resistance, insulation resistance, polarity and wiring checks, RCCB trip testing, socket and point functionality, clamp meter load readings, and a thermal scan of the distribution board. Every value is recorded in your report.
Yes — most of our testing equipment is calibrated by SIRIM Malaysia. Calibration is what turns a reading into evidence, and certificates are available on request.
In many cases yes — we can survey roofs visually and, where appropriate, with drone assistance. If any area genuinely cannot be assessed safely, we say so in the report rather than leaving it ambiguous.
No, and we will tell you when it is not. Many hairline cracks are cosmetic and within tolerance. What matters is the width, pattern, location and whether it is moving — which is why some cracks warrant monitoring rather than immediate repair.
For a standard unit an inspection typically takes 2 to 4 hours; landed and commercial properties take longer. The full report follows within a few working days — we confirm the exact timeline in your quotation.
It depends on property type, size and the scope you need, so we quote per property rather than publishing a flat rate. Send us the property type, built-up area and location on WhatsApp and you will get a clear quotation — usually within one working hour.
Message us on WhatsApp or fill in the quotation form on this site. Tell us the property type, location, size and your preferred date — we confirm availability and price before anything is committed.
Every defect found, with photographs, its location, category and severity, together with instrument readings where tests were carried out. Depending on the service, the report also includes repair recommendations, cost estimates or condition ratings.
Yes. Re-inspection verifies each item on your original defect list and records whether it is properly closed, still incomplete, or has produced a new defect. Whether it is bundled into your package or quoted separately depends on the service you take.
Often yes, if they are in the same area and the scope allows. Tell us all the addresses when requesting your quotation and we will plan the schedule around them.
Yes. Our reports are prepared by registered Building Surveyors using calibrated instruments and are structured for submission. We also provide consultation and documentation support for tribunal cases.
First, we document the refusal along with the technical evidence for each disputed defect. If the matter proceeds, that documented record — readings, dated photos and correspondence chronology — becomes the backbone of your claim.
No — we are Building Surveyors, not legal advisers. What we provide is the technical evidence, documentation and consultation on the condition of the property. For legal advice on your claim, consult a qualified legal professional.
Your S&P agreement, the handover documentation, every defect list you submitted with its date, all correspondence with the developer, and each inspection or re-inspection report. The chronology matters as much as the defects themselves.
Yes. If the developer is disputing your defects or has scheduled a session to close them, we can attend with you — defending each item with instrument evidence and verifying repairs before you agree to close anything.
